messages:
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: Paging: latency-slo-breach detected on /v1/stream (p99 > 5s) — severity: page — paging: @oncall
Alex: saw it, joining. p95 jumped from ~120ms -> 1.2s, p99 ~9.5s on the streaming service. Streaming stalls reported by customers.
Maya: me too. Traces show long waits in kv-cache decode path, lots of eviction churn. CPU on workers spiking and io_wait increasing.
Jordan: adding logs: `kv_cache.eviction_count` spiked from 4k/hr -> 70k in the last 15m. Prefill rate also up. Looks like prefill vs decode imbalance.
Li Wei: any recent rollouts to streaming runtime or prefill config? I don't see a deploy in last 24h but there was a model catalog auto-sync at 00:12 UTC.
Alex: not a code deploy. We rolled a quantized model variant last night; could change token lengths and prefill behavior.
Priya: customer impact: Support thread shows streaming stalls for ~15% of requests. Can we estimate error vs timeout? No increased 5xx, just tail latency and stuck SSE chunks.
Jordan: confirmed: transports stay open but no tokens delivered for ~4-10s in p99. Downstream clients time out or show empty streaming windows.
Maya: root cause hypothesis: KV cache fragmentation + heavy prefill workload causes decode threads to stall waiting on cache compaction/eviction IO. Evictions happening during active decodes -> tail latency.
Alex: mitigation plan: 1) throttle/disable prefill for streaming route 2) increase eviction aggressiveness threshold temporarily (force compaction) 3) route traffic to fallback lower-prefill model variant 4) rolling restart of a small subset if necessary.
Li Wei: agree. Which action is fastest? Turning off prefill flag is config flip, no deploy. I can push it.
Priya: please prioritize disabling prefill for the streaming /v1/stream route only. Keep embedding and text endpoints unaffected.
Maya: tagging the admin playbook: admin ops steps below.
Maya: code snippet to flip via admin API:
```
curl -XPOST "https://admin.redwood.internal/configs/streaming" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  -d '{"kv.prefill_enabled": false}'
```
Alex: I'm going to update routing to fallback model variant `redwood-lite-latency` with reduced prefill params for 10% of traffic as a canary.
deploy-bot: Started traffic shift: /v1/stream -> redwood-lite-latency (10%) @ 2118003485
Jordan: monitoring metrics: within 90s after config flip we should see eviction_count decrease and decode_wait latency drop.
Maya: also lowering cache high-water to 65% from 80% to reduce fragmentation. That's a bit riskier but helps compaction windows.
Li Wei: changed `cache.high_water=0.65` via admin. Note: this triggers more frequent compactions but should reduce long-running evictions.
Alex: can someone run a lightweight rolling restart for 10% of stream workers after the config flips? We want to ensure no in-flight corrupted cache pages.
Jordan: I'll take a small pool. Restart command:
```
for id in $(curl -s "http://orchestrator/pools/streamers?env=prod" | jq -r '.ids[]' | head -n 5); do
  curl -XPOST "http://orchestrator/workers/$id/restart"
done
```
Priya: status update to customers: prepping a note, saying we see tail latency on streaming, mitigation in progress, no 5xx errors, temporary routing enabled.
Maya: metrics update — eviction_count down from 70k -> 8k in last 6m; p99 streaming latency dropped from 9.5s -> 1.8s; p95 down to 350ms. Still above baseline but improving.
Alex: nice. Let's keep the prefill disabled until we validate compaction doesn't re-fragment cache. We should also collect a sample of affected requests to build a regression test.
Jordan: I'm dumping a sample trace and saving to /var/tmp/kv_frag_traces/2118003456.json and uploading to the incident folder.
deploy-bot: Traffic shift increased to 25% to redwood-lite-latency @ 2118003540
Li Wei: caution: increased traffic to fallback may raise overall token cost. Watch cost alerts.
Priya: Customer comms sent: "We're mitigating a streaming tail latency issue; routing to a lower-latency model for some requests; investigating root cause; will follow up." :email:
Maya: next steps: 1) run offline eviction simulation against current key distribution 2) add guardrails on prefill concurrency 3) improve telemetry to surface prefill vs decode imbalance earlier.
Alex: agree. Also add an alert for `kv.prefill_rate / kv.decode_rate > 1.5` — that'll catch imbalance.
Jordan: logging a follow-up ticket: INF-3742 "Investigate cache fragmentation and prefill/decode scheduling". Assigning to eng-runtime and eng-sre.
Priya: handoff: I'm on until 2315 UTC, leaving pager to Jordan after that. Jordan, please take the on-call at 2315 and keep monitoring until all metrics back to baseline.
Jordan: taking handoff. Will keep an eye on p99 and eviction_count. Please ping if you see customer regressions.
Alex: :thumbsup: thanks team. Leaving channels open for follow-up notes.
oncall-bot: Incident acknowledged: severity reduced to degraded service. Updated incident timeline with mitigation actions. Incident ID: INC-2026-2118003456
